punchline: Wharton's youngest full professor got there partly by telling his inbox, politely, to wait.
thirty_sec: Cal Newport's Deep Work describes Adam Grant, Wharton's youngest full professor and a prolific publisher. Grant packed all his teaching into one semester and used the other for research. During research stretches he disappeared for several days behind an email auto-responder. The surprise is that he was also known for being generous and keeping his door open. He just did the helping and the deep thinking at separate, scheduled times, so focus multiplied what his hours produced.
question: When did you last spend several hours on one hard problem with no way for anyone to interrupt you?
